Sensetal App

Health · Mobile

Sensetal App

Product DesignUX ResearchInformation ArchitectureUser InterfaceMobile
industryHealth
clientSensetal
duration4 months
year2025
Challenge

Sensetal is a B2B healthtech company offering a workplace wellness and self-care app for organizations with 500+ employees. Despite its strong potential, the app faced criticism for its incomplete appearance, low usability, instability, and poor user engagement. The challenge was to transform both the visual and functional experience of the app — improving its appeal, usability, and perceived value for both employees and the companies that purchase it.

Objectives
  1. Improve the usability and aesthetics of the application
  2. Engage and retain users, increasing continued use
  3. Make the app more appealing and sellable to companies
  4. Optimize pain markers, workout flows, routines, and light gamification
My Role

I served as the UX Designer responsible for the experience strategy and product delivery. I led every step of the UX process — from research and discovery through ideation, wireframes, and final UI.

Tools

Miro · Figma · Google Workspace

Discovery & Stakeholder Kick-off

I started with a kick-off session with stakeholders to understand business objectives, the client companies' context, and initial hypotheses. I used a CSD Matrix (Certainties, Assumptions, Doubts) to map out investigation paths.

Qualitative Research

I conducted in-depth interviews with 6 users. Key goals:
• Understand motivations and barriers to using the app
• Investigate how the app fit into their work and wellness routines
• Identify usability problems and engagement opportunities

Key findings:
• Confusing UI and unfinished appearance
• Long, friction-heavy onboarding
• Poorly functional pain markers
• Low understanding of workplace wellness benefits
• Selective interest in gamification
• Difficulty integrating the app into the daily work routine

I developed two key personas to build empathy and guide ideation toward more personalized solutions.

Ideation & Strategy

I facilitated a co-creation session with stakeholders, mapping key problems and collaboratively voting on priorities. Based on prioritized problems, I ran ideation sessions using brainstorming and affinity mapping. This led to:
• User flows for key paths (onboarding, workouts, performance, gamification)
• Proposals for engagement groups
• Feature prioritization and improvement roadmap

Information Architecture

I built a content inventory that aligned UX, UI, and development — detailing each flow's objectives, user stories, expected inputs, planned components, and key insights.

Wireframes

I created low-fidelity wireframes for all prioritized features:
• Simplified onboarding
• Personalized workouts better integrated into the work day
• Redesigned pain marker experience
• Home screen with strategic shortcuts
• Performance page with visual statistics
• Light, motivational gamification

User Interface

After aligning the visual direction with the client, I delivered:
• Visual concept (typography, colors, style)
• Design tokens and spacing rules
• Component library in Figma
• High-fidelity screens with dev documentation
• Structured handoff with navigable prototypes and behavior specs

Results

• Professional, modern, and commercially strong visual identity
• Significantly improved usability — more intuitive and lightweight
• Reformulated workout and pain marker experiences for clarity and engagement
• Light gamification with the "Rhythm Loop", rankings, and realistic rewards stimulated continued use

Reflections & Learnings

This project was an excellent exercise in strategic UX with a product vision. Working with a wellness app in a corporate context required sensitivity to balance business needs, technical constraints, and users' real daily routines. It was rewarding to see the client's perception shift about the power of design — not just visually, but functionally and commercially.

Prime Unimed

Healthcare · Enterprise SaaS

Prime Unimed

Product DesignUX ResearchInformation ArchitectureUser InterfaceDesign System
industryHealthcare
clientUnimed
duration4 months
year2025
Challenge

The PRIMe system, used by providers in the Unimed network, had serious usability, performance, and visual obsolescence issues. Its use required extensive training, it made tasks difficult to complete, and it discouraged adoption. The challenge was to make PRIME a modern, attractive, intuitive, and commercially viable system — focusing on ease of use, fewer steps, and improved workflows.

Objectives
  1. Reduce the complexity of using the system
  2. Make the interface more attractive and commercially appealing
  3. Make flows simpler and faster
My Role

I served as a participating designer, actively contributing to strategy, research, information architecture, interface design, and Design System creation. I led interviews, heuristic evaluations, requirements gathering, wireframes, and prototypes in Figma. I collaborated with the technical team and stakeholders throughout.

Tools

Miro · Figma · Google Workspace

Discovery & Immersion

I ran stakeholder interviews to understand the system's structure and goals, map existing functionality, and surface the key problems users reported. Through a walthrough I explored the platform firsthand and identified usability issues: long flows, excessive clicks, navigation problems, absent feedback, and visual inconsistency across screens.

Research

I structured a quantitative research plan using a CSD Matrix, then designed an online structured survey to identify:
• Which features were most used in the registration module
• Main difficulties and pain points
• Unexplored opportunities

We received 40 responses with a strong distribution across system users.

Key findings:
• System perceived as complex and hard to use
• Long, fragmented flows making simple tasks hard to complete
• Filters difficult to use and ineffective
• Desire for a home screen with indicators and shortcuts for frequent tasks

Information Architecture

Based on research, I mapped the main flows and tasks using:
• Content inventory with tasks, components, and user stories
• User flows for ideal paths through priority tasks
• Navigation restructured around jobs-to-be-done
• Grouping of actions on single pages, simplifying the registration flow

Wireframes & Prototyping

Wireframes were built in Figma focused on the Provider Registration area, including:
• Optimized tables and filters
• Simplified provider registration consolidated into a single flow
• Home screen with indicators, recent reports, and a customizable shortcut area

UI & Design System

After wireframe validation, I started the UI phase with a visual brief aligned with the Unimed team. Using the Angular library as a base, I adapted the design kit with the brand's visual tokens. I created a Design System with 27+ components and variants, including PRIME-specific business components. All screens were documented and delivered for development with ongoing technical team alignment.

Results

• Modern interface, simpler and more efficient system, with positive user feedback
• Dramatic reduction in time to complete tasks like viewing or registering providers
• Home screen with indicators, reports, and shortcuts improved the overall experience
• System is currently in implementation with ongoing support

Reflections & Learnings

Applying the full UX process was essential to transforming the PRIME system into a more usable, modern, and appealing platform. By grounding prioritization in user research, we created solutions centered on real tasks and real problems. This project was a valuable lesson in applying UX methods to large, complex systems with multiple areas and stakeholders.

Vendavall

E-commerce · SaaS

Vendavall

Information ArchitectureUser InterfaceMobileMicrointeractionsUX Writing
industryMarketing / Incentive
clientMarkUp
duration4 months
year2025
Challenge

MarkUp, an agency specializing in incentive marketing, was losing key clients to competitors with more modern, simple, and efficient platforms. Their Vendavall platform — which runs their campaigns — needed to become more visually attractive, easier to use, and adaptable for multiple clients (white-label model), in order to reduce churn, support sales, and increase engagement.

Objectives
  1. Make the Vendavall platform more modern, functional, and visually attractive
  2. Reduce churn and increase commercial conversion
  3. Improve usability and deliver a good mobile experience
  4. Structure the product as a scalable, customizable SaaS system
My Role

I served as UX and Product Designer, leading the entire experience front of the platform — from investigating problems with users and stakeholders, through information architecture, flows, wireframes, and visual interface delivery with a design system.

Tools

Miro · Figma · Google Workspace

Discovery & Immersion

I conducted stakeholder interviews (commercial and support teams) to raise hypotheses and map pain points:
• Difficulty navigating for users with low digital literacy
• High volume of support tickets for login/password confusion
• Outdated visuals making conversion and retention harder
• Mobile use was common, but the platform wasn't responsive

I mapped the current journey to understand the path customers and users took from acquisition through daily use, and created three proto-personas based on usage profiles (managers and salespeople with different digital literacy levels).

Information Architecture & System Mapping

I mapped the entire current system and the areas to be addressed in the first deliveries. I analyzed the existing first-access flow to identify bottlenecks and friction points.

Wireframes & Priority Flows

I developed mobile and desktop wireframes focused initially on login, registration, and the home screen. I used a conversational approach, progress bars, and clear language. I reformulated the token verification step — renaming it to "code" and including tutorial videos.

Mobile was a critical gap: the platform had no mobile version, preventing participants from interacting on the device they actually used most. Making all interactions work on mobile was a major win for MarkUp.

For registration (a major pain point), I proposed a conversational, step-by-step interaction — more explanatory and clearer than a static form.

For UX Writing, I rethought terms like "token" in registration, and simplified language across the platform to be more accessible for users with lower digital literacy.

User Interface & Design System

After receiving MarkUp's visual concept, I adapted the UI based on the Tailwind framework and a scalable design system:
• Palette with 3 core colors + neutrals and feedback colors, in dark and light tonal variants for white-label flexibility
• Reusable components aligned with the dev team, using Tailwind as the base
• Special areas like Avatars and Games with custom, more playful layouts
• AI-generated soundtracks (via Suno) and foley sounds for the Roulette and Scratch Card games
• All core platform areas designed: balance, statements, performance, point distribution, rankings, games, avatars, news, library, training, surveys, and profile
• A lightweight design system, compatible with Tailwind and applicable for white-label use across multiple MarkUp clients

Metrics Framework

As a strategic part of the project, I defined the metrics to be tracked — organized around three pillars: acquisition, engagement, and churn. For each metric, I specified what to measure, how to measure it, data sources, and tracking frequency. This gave MarkUp a foundation for their first steps toward a data-driven culture.

Results

• New design already being used in commercial presentations with success
• Prospects began to see value in the product, increasing conversions
• Existing clients showed satisfaction with the improvements
• A significant portion of the system has already been implemented

Reflections & Learnings

This project consolidated my role as a product designer, going beyond UI to structure a scalable system. MarkUp has deep expertise as a marketing agency, and this project contributed to forming a product culture and creating a solid foundation for innovation. Key learnings: the importance of considering different digital literacy levels in design, and the value of simple, clear, accessible language to engage diverse audiences.

Flexpro — SIMOB

PropTech · SaaS

Flexpro — SIMOB

Product DesignUX ResearchInformation ArchitectureUser InterfaceDesign SystemUX Mentoring
industryReal Estate SaaS
clientFlexpro
duration3 months
year2023
Challenge

SIMOB is a CRM system developed by Flexpro for real estate companies, supporting rental management, client tracking, and financials. I was invited to lead the complete redesign of the financial module, which suffered from poor usability, an outdated interface, and near-zero engagement. Beyond the UX challenge, the project included mentoring junior designers at Flexpro to strengthen the design culture and build internal capability.

Objectives
  1. Redesign the financial module experience with a user-centered approach
  2. Improve usability, data clarity, and operational efficiency
  3. Engage and retain real estate industry clients
  4. Support the formation of a more strategic internal design team
My Role

I was the UX Lead responsible for the experience strategy and product delivery. I led every stage — from research through wireframes and final UI. I also served as a UX mentor for the client's design team, creating support materials and facilitating sessions on UX process and approaches.

Tools

Miro · Figma · Google Workspace

Discovery & Immersion

I started with a detailed kick-off with Flexpro stakeholders and leadership. Through these conversations, I understood the product's history, market demands, and the main reasons for low adoption of the financial module. I evaluated the existing screens and raised initial hypotheses using a CSD Matrix (Certainties, Assumptions, Doubts).

Research

I structured a mixed research plan:
• Qualitative: 9 in-depth interviews with financial module users from small and large real estate firms
• Quantitative: 30 survey responses on usage patterns, difficulties, and expectations

Key findings:
• Users didn't know how to use the module in practice
• Lack of clarity in data and processes
• Features scattered across multiple modules
• Preference for spreadsheets as a faster alternative
• Bank reconciliation and reporting didn't meet actual needs

Ideation & Strategy

We ran co-ideation sessions with the Flexpro team, voting on key problems and prototyping solutions based on team ideas and research insights. Prioritized ideas:
• Financial dashboard with real estate health indicators
• Home screen with quick actions and customizable shortcuts
• New bank reconciliation flow with file import
• Intuitive screens for transfers, bill generation, and statements
• Consolidated account and report view

Information Architecture

Based on prioritized solutions, I mapped the new information architecture. I built a content inventory and, for each functional area, created user stories with objectives, tasks, and required components.

Wireframes

Low and high-fidelity wireframes were built in Figma alongside Flexpro's designers. Key screens included:
• Customizable financial dashboard with indicators and reports
• Guided bank reconciliation flow with integration
• Account and statement view with filters and period detail
• Home screen with widgets and shortcuts for frequent tasks

User Interface

After wireframe validation, I ran a visual brief with the client to align tone, identity, and interface direction. I then developed:
• Visual concept and product identity
• Design tokens: colors, typography, spacing
• Reusable components with states and variations
• Documentation and Figma handoff for the development team

Design Culture & Mentoring

Throughout the project, I focused on developing Flexpro's design team. I ran training sessions on:
• UX Research
• Information Architecture
• Usability Testing
• Wireframes and Prototyping
• Using Figma for documentation and handoff

Deliveries were made collaboratively, involving junior designers in the project execution.

Results

• The financial module became far more intuitive and functional
• Reduced dependence on spreadsheets and external systems
• The new visual experience increased engagement with the tool
• Dashboards and reconciliation flows expanded analytical and decision-making power
• The design team strengthened and began applying learnings across other initiatives
• This project marked the beginning of a broader transformation in Flexpro's product and design culture

Reflections & Learnings

This project let me operate across multiple fronts: user research, interfaces, and building a design system. It was also a special opportunity to serve as a mentor, accompanying junior designers and helping them apply UX best practices in a real, complex project. Seeing how UX can generate organizational impact — encouraging internal teams to mature their design practice and put users at the center — was deeply rewarding.

Becomex — Feed de Negócios

B2B · Data Product

Becomex — Feed de Negócios

Product DesignUX ResearchInformation ArchitectureUser InterfaceDesign SystemDesign Lead
industryTax Technology
clientBecomex
duration2 years
year2023–2025
Challenge

Becomex, traditionally focused on strategic consulting around tax incentive regimes, sought to take an important step toward digitalization: transforming internal data into a scalable, innovative product capable of generating continuous value, attracting new clients, and repositioning the company as a product-oriented organization. The challenge was to develop the company's first digital product — the Business Feed — uniting data intelligence, user experience, and commercial potential.

Objectives
  1. Transform incentive regime data into a strategic, interactive platform
  2. Engage Becomex's clients and suppliers, activating network effects and acquiring new accounts
  3. Increase retention and generate new business opportunities
  4. Create a scalable product with a more digital business model
My Role

I served as Design Lead on the project, leading the design team and collaborating with Becomex's strategic stakeholders. My responsibilities included defining the strategic vision and UX direction, facilitating workshops and interviews, structuring research and personas, creating flows, prototypes, and the Design System, and aligning product, business, and technology.

Tools

Miro · Figma · Hey Marvin · Google Workspace

Discovery & Immersion

We started with in-depth stakeholder interviews to understand Becomex's business model, internal pain points, strategic goals, and relationships with suppliers and clients. This deep dive was essential to align expectations and map initial hypotheses.

Qualitative Research

Based on immersion, I structured a research plan focused on:
• Understanding the business moment (product in ideation phase)
• Mapping different profiles in the chain (clients and suppliers)
• Identifying value drivers and potential features

I used in-depth interviews with an extreme-profile matrix and built a CSD Matrix to structure the interview guide for each profile. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed with HeyMarvin's AI support, resulting in strategic personas for the product.

Key research insights:
• Distinct profiles between clients and suppliers, with specific pain points
• Need for greater visibility into indicators
• High value placed on features that enhance supplier competitiveness

I developed two key personas to build empathy and guide ideation toward more personalized solutions.

Ideation & Strategy

We ran co-creation sessions with stakeholders and the internal team to propose solutions for problems identified in research. Ideas were prioritized by feasibility vs. impact, leading to a proposed navigation structure and MVP feature set.

Information Architecture

The architecture was defined from priority flows and value hypotheses, with emphasis on:
• The home screen, displaying key indicators and business opportunities
• Visibility of cost-reduction proposals and action plans

I created low-fidelity wireframes in Miro, consolidating ideas from the research phase. Given the product's novelty and informational complexity, the validation session with low-fi wireframes was essential to conceive the solution in its earliest form. After validation, we moved to Figma with real data to develop high-fidelity wireframes.

Interface & Design System

The visual design was built on the Ant Design library, per the development team's guidance:
• Visual brief with the marketing and technology teams
• Visual concept creation and application across screens
• Color, typography, and component token definition

The Design System — called Shield — was designed to be scalable and evolutionary, with reusable components aligned to Becomex's brand identity. Beyond Ant Design component customization, I designed business components to support the specific interactions proposed in the solution.

Results

• Product validated with stakeholders and presented at a Becomex client event — positive feedback received
• New strategic approach to supplier relationships, incentivizing platform adoption
• A product with scale potential and new monetization models
• A structured foundation for future digital products at Becomex

The Business Feed was Becomex's first UX project — and given its success, strategic stakeholders initiated new UX projects, in which I continued to lead and execute. This pioneering project structured the Design stack for subsequent initiatives, and the new visual and Design System were widely embraced by Becomex.

Reflections & Learnings

This project was fundamental in consolidating my role as a product strategist and design leader. Key learnings: the importance of research in defining value; how to structure MVPs in complex contexts; and how to translate research insights into product visuals and interactions. Over two years at Becomex, I worked across different products and features — strengthening my practice alongside strategic and development teams, applying varied frameworks and processes, and running experiments to validate solutions.
